item.title: DPRK Cyber Threat Highlights — 30-Day Look Back
item.description: Executive Summary Open-source reporting over the past thirty days shows continued, multi-pronged North Korean (DPRK) cyber activity pressing against South Korean government, defense-adjacent, financial, and software-supply-chain targets, with clear implications for any network that interconnects with Republic of Korea (ROK) government or U.S. Forces Korea infrastructure, including systems that feed into the Korea theater portion of the Department of Defense Information Network (DoDIN-K). Four threads stand out: A joint advisory from four South Korean security agencies formally linked the Lazarus Group to the Guntra ransomware operation, describing shared infrastructure and hosting and laying out an active wateringhole campaign against Korean websites.
